newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for Jan 16.

text.p: All Mexican ports were open early Thursday, the Communications and Transport Ministry said in its daily 1000 local/1600 GMT report .
Crude shipping ports Dos Bocas and Pajaritos were reopened Wednesday as wind speeds died down, although a weak cold front could threaten Gulf of Mexico ports again, the ministry said.
The largest of Mexico's crude ports, Cayo Arcas in Campeche state, remained open for petroleum shipping through the week's high winds and waves.

Pajaritos ships an average 400,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude and Dos Bocas exports 300,000 bpd, according to the latest oil and gas monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) statistics. Cayo Arcas ships an average 600,000 bpd.
Puerto Madero, Alvarado, Tuxpan, Veracruz and Coatzacoalcos ports were closed to smaller boats amid winds between 15 and 45 km per hour.
The report also warned against smaller ships sailing along the coasts of Tamaulipas and Veracruz because of winds and high waves.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Gulf of Mexico, Caribbean and Pacific Coast.

Possibility of light rains along coast of southern Baja California, Sonora, Sinaloa, Tepic, Jalisco, Colima and Michoacan. Winds from the northwest at 10 to 15 knots (19 to 28 km/11 to 17 miles per hour) and waves three to five feet high, except in the Gulf of Tehuantepec where winds were reported from the northeast.

A weak cold front moving southwest across the country's northeast and southeast Gulf of Mexico region with light drops in temperature, clouds and disperse rains along the coasts of Tamaulipas and Veracruz, with winds from the north at 20 to 25 knots (38 to 47 km/22 to 28 miles per hour) and waves at six to eight feet during the next 24 hours.

Moderate convective activity along the northeast Caribbean sea, light clouds and possible showers along the Central American coasts, with winds from the east and northeast at 10 to 15 knots and waves three to five feet high.
